title: op-amp积分器：方波变三角波
summary: LM358（单电源 9 V）搭反相积分器：方波输入变成三角波输出，由三角波的斜率测出 RC。
concepts: DC feedback resistor 直流反馈电阻
description: 单电源 9 V。RB1、RB2（10 kΩ）把 IN+ 定在 4.5 V；信号发生器 → CIN（10 µF）→ RIN（10 kΩ）→ IN−；CF（100 nF）和 RP（100 kΩ）并联在 IN− 和 OUT 之间。CH1 看信号发生器，CH2 看 OUT。

cards.title: 方波进去，看出来什么
text: - **电源**：9 V 接 LM358 的 8 脚，GND 接 4 脚。**偏置**：RB1、RB2（都是 **`10 kΩ`**）从 +9 V 到 GND 分压，中点接 **IN+**。
- **输入**：信号发生器 → **CIN `10 µF`** → **RIN `10 kΩ`** → **IN−**。**反馈**：**CF `100 nF`** 接在 IN− 和 OUT 之间，**RP `100 kΩ`** 和 CF 并联。
- 方波、**`1 kHz`**、幅度 **`1 V`**、偏置 **`0 V`**。CH1 看信号发生器，CH2 看 OUT。
输出是什么形状？输入为正的时候，它往哪边走？

cards.title: 电流全部流进电容
text: - 负反馈让 IN− 跟着 IN+ 停在 4.5 V。输入电阻里的电流 i = v_in / RIN 不受输出影响，又进不了 op-amp（运算放大器），只能**全部流进 CF**。
- 恒定的电流给电容充电，电容电压就**匀速**变化（3.3 的 dv/dt = i / C）。输出跟着电容电压走，方向相反：
$$\frac{dv_o}{dt} = -\frac{v_{in}}{R_{IN} C_F} = -\frac{1 V}{10 kΩ × 100 nF}$$
![](fig:integ)
- 方波每半个周期输入不变，输出就是一条斜线：方波变成三角波。和 RC 积分电路不同，这里的斜率一直准确，输出也可以做大。
![](fig:tri)

cards.title: 量斜率，看辅助元件
text: - **`1 kHz`** 方波：读 OUT 三角波的峰峰值，算出 RIN·CF；万用表直流档量 OUT 的中心。
- 再试 **`100 Hz`**：半个周期变长，三角波的边开始变弯。
- 三个辅助元件：**RB1、RB2** 把参考点抬到 4.5 V，单电源的输出才能上下摆；**CIN** 挡住信号发生器和 IN− 之间 4.5 V 的直流差；**RP** 给直流一条反馈的路，否则一点点直流误差也会被一直积分，输出撞到电源就不动了。

cards.title: 带走
text: - **op-amp（运算放大器）积分器**：dv_o/dt = −v_in / (RIN·CF)。方波 → 三角波，正弦 → 余弦。
- **虚短 + 虚断**让电阻电流不受输出影响，所以它在很宽的频率范围里都是真正的积分。
- **RP 不能少**：没有它，直流误差会把输出推到电源轨。代价是频率很低时不再像积分。
- **真实电路里**：10 µF 的 CIN 一般是电解电容，+ 脚朝直流电位高的一侧（这里是 RIN / IN− 那边）。LM358 的输入只到约 V+ − 1.5 V，IN+ 在 4.5 V 没问题。

caption.text: i 穿过 RIN 后只能流进 CF。IN+ 接在 4.5 V 的参考点 V_REF 上；RP 很大，只管直流。

i18n.en: After RIN, i can only flow into CF. IN+ sits on the 4.5 V reference V_REF; RP is large and only matters for DC.

caption.text: 虚线：输入方波；实线：输出减去 4.5 V。输入为正时输出匀速下降，为负时匀速上升。

i18n.en: Dashed: the input square wave; solid: the output minus 4.5 V. While the input is positive the output falls steadily; while negative it rises.

en.startNote: **Half-built**: the battery, the LM358's supply pins, bias resistors RB1/RB2 (IN+ = 4.5 V), the function generator, DC-blocking CIN and both probes are wired. **Why**: single-supply biasing is a helper trick (explained under "Why the helper parts are needed"); the integrator itself is RIN and CF. **Your job**: add RIN (10kΩ, CIN → pin 2 IN−), CF (100nF, pin 2 → pin 1 OUT) and RP (100kΩ) in parallel with CF.
en.title: The op-amp integrator: square in, triangle out
en.summary: An inverting integrator on an LM358 (single 9 V supply): a square wave in, a triangle out; the triangle's slope measures RC.
en.description: Single 9 V supply. RB1 and RB2 (10 kΩ) hold IN+ at 4.5 V; generator → CIN (10 µF) → RIN (10 kΩ) → IN−; CF (100 nF) and RP (100 kΩ) in parallel between IN− and OUT. CH1 on the generator, CH2 on OUT.
en.compare:
**Compare**: with a ±1 V square, the output ramps at a constant 1 V / (10 kΩ × 100 nF) = 1000 V/s in each half; half a period, 0.5 ms, covers 0.5 V: **a 0.5 Vpp triangle centred on 4.5 V**, falling while the input is positive. If the output sticks at 7.5 V or 0 V, check that the feedback goes to IN− and that RP is in place.

- 2 kHz square: same slope, half the time, so the Vpp halves to about 0.25 V.
- 1 kHz sine (1 V amplitude): the output is a sine of the same frequency, amplitude 1 V / (ωRC) ≈ 0.16 V (about 0.32 Vpp).
- 100 Hz square: half a period, 5 ms, is comparable with RP·CF = 10 ms; the sides turn into exponentials and Vpp ≈ **4.9 V**, far below the 10 V of an ideal integral.
hints: Bias: RB1 from +9 V to IN+, RB2 from IN+ to GND.
Input: generator → CIN → RIN → IN−; CF and RP both span IN− to OUT.
Slope = input voltage / (RIN·CF); half a period covers one peak-to-peak.
tests: 1 kHz square: a triangle centred on VREF
2 kHz square: half the time, half the triangle height
1 kHz sine: the integral of a sine is a (cosine-shaped) sine
100 Hz square: RP shows, less than an ideal integral, no clipping

measurements.explain: Slope 1 V / (RIN·CF) = 1000 V/s; half a period, 0.5 ms, covers 0.5 V.

measurements.ask: Half a period, 0.5 ms, covers one peak-to-peak: from your reading, RIN·CF = 1 V × 0.5 ms / Vpp
measurements.explain: 10 kΩ × 100 nF = 1 ms. The op-amp keeps the resistor current independent of the output, so the slope is always input / RC.

measurements.ask: Same state: OUT to GND on the multimeter's DC range (the triangle's centre)
measurements.explain: IN− follows IN+ = 4.5 V; RP gives DC feedback and the input averages 0, so the centre is 4.5 V.

measurements.ask: On the scope: during the positive half of the input, which way does the output go?
measurements.explain: The current v_in / RIN flows into IN− and on into CF, pulling the OUT side down.

measurements.ask: 100 Hz square: OUT's peak-to-peak (compare with the 10 V of an ideal integral)
measurements.explain: Half a period, 5 ms, is now comparable with RP·CF = 10 ms, so RP shows: 2 × 10 × tanh(T / (4·RP·CF)) ≈ 4.9 V.

cards.title: Square wave in — what comes out?
text: - **Supply**: 9 V to LM358 pin 8, GND to pin 4. **Bias**: RB1 and RB2 (both **`10 kΩ`**) divide +9 V to GND; their midpoint goes to **IN+**.
- **Input**: generator → **CIN `10 µF`** → **RIN `10 kΩ`** → **IN−**. **Feedback**: **CF `100 nF`** between IN− and OUT, with **RP `100 kΩ`** in parallel.
- Square, **`1 kHz`**, amplitude **`1 V`**, offset **`0 V`**. CH1 on the generator, CH2 on OUT.
What shape is the output? Which way does it go while the input is positive?

cards.title: All the current goes into the capacitor
text: - Negative feedback keeps IN− at IN+'s 4.5 V. The current in the input resistor, i = v_in / RIN, doesn't depend on the output and can't enter the op-amp, so **all of it flows into CF**.
- A steady current charges a capacitor at a **steady rate** (dv/dt = i / C from 3.3). The output follows the capacitor voltage, in the opposite direction:
$$\frac{dv_o}{dt} = -\frac{v_{in}}{R_{IN} C_F} = -\frac{1 V}{10 kΩ × 100 nF}$$
![](fig:integ)
- In each half of the square wave the input is constant, so the output is a straight ramp: the square becomes a triangle. Unlike the RC integrator, the slope stays exact and the output can be large.
![](fig:tri)

cards.title: Measure the slope, look at the helpers
text: - **`1 kHz`** square: read OUT's triangle peak-to-peak and work out RIN·CF; measure OUT's centre on the multimeter's DC range.
- Then try **`100 Hz`**: with longer halves the triangle's sides start to bend.

- Three helpers: **RB1, RB2** lift the reference to 4.5 V so a single-supply output can swing both ways; **CIN** blocks the 4.5 V DC difference between the generator and IN−; **RP** gives DC a feedback path — without it the tiniest DC error is integrated on and on until the output hits a supply rail and stays there.

cards.title: Take away
text: - **Op-amp integrator**: dv_o/dt = −v_in / (RIN·CF). Square → triangle, sine → cosine.
- **Virtual short + no input current** keep the resistor current independent of the output, so it integrates properly over a wide range of frequencies.
- **RP is a must**: without it DC errors push the output into a rail. The price: at very low frequencies it stops behaving like an integrator.

- **In a real circuit**: a 10 µF CIN is usually electrolytic; its + leg faces the higher DC potential (here the RIN / IN− side). The LM358's inputs work up to about V+ − 1.5 V, so IN+ at 4.5 V is fine.

tests.name: 1 kHz 方波：三角波，中心在 VREF
2 kHz 方波：时间减半，三角波高度减半
1 kHz 正弦：正弦的积分还是正弦（余弦）
100 Hz 方波：RP 的影响显现，比理想积分小，且不削顶

compare:
**对比**：方波 ±1 V 时，每半个周期输出以恒定斜率 1 V / (10 kΩ × 100 nF) = 1000 V/s 变化，半个周期 0.5 ms 走 0.5 V：**0.5 Vpp 的三角波，中心 4.5 V**，输入为正时输出下降。如果输出贴在 7.5 V 或 0 V 不动，检查反馈是否接到 IN−、RP 有没有接上。

- 2 kHz 方波：斜率不变，时间减半，Vpp 减半到约 0.25 V。
- 1 kHz 正弦（幅度 1 V）：输出是同频正弦，幅度 1 V / (ωRC) ≈ 0.16 V（约 0.32 Vpp）。
- 100 Hz 方波：半个周期 5 ms 已和 RP·CF = 10 ms 相当，边变成指数曲线，Vpp ≈ **4.9 V**，比理想积分的 10 V 小得多。

measurements.ask: 1 kHz 方波：CH2（OUT）三角波的峰峰值
measurements.explain: 斜率 1 V / (RIN·CF) = 1000 V/s，半个周期 0.5 ms 走 0.5 V。

measurements.ask: 半个周期 0.5 ms 走完一个峰峰值：用你的读数算 RIN·CF = 1 V × 0.5 ms / Vpp
measurements.explain: 10 kΩ × 100 nF = 1 ms。op-amp（运算放大器）让电阻电流不受输出影响，所以斜率始终是输入 / RC。

measurements.ask: 同一状态：万用表直流档测 OUT 对 GND（三角波的中心）
measurements.explain: IN− 跟着 IN+ = 4.5 V；RP 给直流提供反馈，输入的平均值是 0，所以中心就在 4.5 V。

measurements.ask: 在示波器上看：输入为正的半个周期里，输出往哪边走？
measurements.explain: 电流 v_in / RIN 从输入流进 IN−，全部流进 CF，把 OUT 那一侧往下拉。

measurements.ask: 100 Hz 方波：OUT 的峰峰值（和“理想积分”的 10 V 比）
measurements.explain: 半个周期 5 ms 已经和 RP·CF = 10 ms 差不多，RP 的影响出来了：2 × 10 × tanh(T / (4·RP·CF)) ≈ 4.9 V。

hints: 偏置：RB1 从 +9 V 到 IN+，RB2 从 IN+ 到 GND。
输入：信号发生器 → CIN → RIN → IN−；CF 和 RP 都跨在 IN− 和 OUT 之间。
斜率 = 输入电压 / (RIN·CF)；半个周期走完一个峰峰值。
startNote: **半成品**：电池、LM358 的电源脚、偏置电阻 RB1/RB2（IN+ = 4.5 V）、信号发生器、隔直电容 CIN 和两个探头都已接好。**为什么**：单电源偏置是辅助技巧，下面“为什么需要这些辅助元件”讲了它；积分器本身是 RIN 和 CF。**你要做**：加上 RIN（10kΩ，CIN → 2 脚 IN−）、CF（100nF，2 脚 → 1 脚 OUT）和与 CF 并联的 RP（100kΩ）。
